description: Open an http(s) URL in the current tab. Returns evidence and a snapshot of the visible screen (elements carry refs like e12), with counts of what is above and below; snapshot:false leaves the screen out for a page you will only read or leave. Words like cheapest, latest, highest-rated or most mean the site's own sort or tab for that order (a list's default order is usually something else, e.g. 'Best' or 'Featured'): open that tab or choose that sort (a label naming its best value is not the list), read the top, and say in the answer which sort, tab and filters it came from. The top is the answer only when that order ranks by what the task asks over everything inside its bounds; otherwise say how much was read and call the pick the best of those read, not the best. Break a tie in that order only by what the task asks; otherwise report the tie. Search, sort and filter addresses: you may build one from the task's own words (a query, a place, dates, a sort, a bound) or change a parameter this site has shown you in an address or link (browser_query gives a link's full href), its page number included. A search the site's form takes several steps for (a place, dates, guests, a sort, filters) is usually one call as such an address, where the form takes a call and a screen for each step. Before you use its results, check on the page that what you meant was applied: the heading, breadcrumb, selected sort or filter, and the results themselves (each one you count inside the bound); never the address or a search box, which can repeat a value the site ignored. When they do not match or a bound cannot be checked, use the site's own form, or say in the answer what could not be applied. Never write a sign-in, session, account, identity or tracking value yourself (tokens, ids, codes): keep one only as the site gave it, or leave it out. Over several sites, finish one and note the values the next needs before opening it. A task that names no site: search the web first with your own search tool to pick the site, or answer from the search when that is enough; open a site when the task needs one (a price for dates, a form, an account).

snapshot.description: Default true. Choose by your next step on this page: false when you will only read it (browser_query, browser_get_text) or go on to another URL; keep true when you will click, type or choose on it (you need its refs). false still returns the evidence (where it landed, the title, what was added or removed), loading notes and anything that needs a person; browser_snapshot shows the screen at any time.
